sources.title: WCAG 3.0 Working Draft (March 2026)
sources.description: W3C Working Draft — outcomes-based conformance model, not yet a Recommendation. Candidate Recommendation expected Q4 2027; W3C Recommendation not before late 2029. Do not gate products against this draft; use WCAG 2.2 AA.

sources.title: WebAIM Million 2025
sources.description: Annual scan of 1,000,000 home pages (February 2025): 95.9% had detectable WCAG failures; 79.1% had low-contrast text; average 51 errors per page. Pages using ARIA averaged 34.2% more errors — prefer native HTML semantics.

sources.title: EN 301 549 V3.2.1 — European ICT Accessibility Standard (current)
sources.description: Current harmonized European standard for ICT accessibility (March 2021) — references WCAG 2.1 AA. V4.1.1 (incorporating WCAG 2.2 AA) had a public-review draft (v4.1.0) released November 2025; publication in the Official Journal of the EU expected around October 2026 (unverified as of 2026-07-11 — EU/ETSI publication timelines have slipped before). Audit against WCAG 2.2 now to avoid a re-audit gap when V4.1.1 is adopted.

sources.title: European Accessibility Act (EAA)
sources.description: EU directive (2019/882) requiring accessibility for in-scope products and services, conformance via EN 301 549. Enforcement ACTIVE since 28 June 2025 for new and substantially-modified services (active enforcement underway — e.g. French legal notices and Nov 2025 injunctions); existing services have a transitional period until 28 June 2030. Native mobile apps are in scope as software. Ongoing obligation, not a cleared past deadline.

sources.title: ADA.gov — Web Accessibility Guidance
sources.description: US Department of Justice guidance on ADA web accessibility obligations. Title II applies only to state/local government; Title III (private business) has no DOJ technical-standard rule or fixed deadline.

sources.title: Federal Register — Extension of Compliance Dates, ADA Title II Web and Mobile App Accessibility Rule
sources.description: DOJ Interim Final Rule, effective 20 April 2026, extending ADA Title II web/mobile-app compliance dates by one year: population 50,000+ now 26 April 2027 (was 24 April 2026); population under 50,000 or special districts now 26 April 2028 (was 24 April 2027). Underlying technical standard remains WCAG 2.1 Level AA (final rule adopted 24 April 2024). Comment period closed 22 June 2026 — verify before citing as final.

sources.title: Section508.gov — Applicability & Conformance Requirements
sources.description: US federal ICT accessibility standard. Current binding technical standard is WCAG 2.0 Level AA (2017 refresh) — has not been updated to reference WCAG 2.1 or 2.2. Target 2.2 AA as forward cover, but 2.0 AA is the current legal baseline.

sources.title: UsableNet — 2025 Midyear Digital Accessibility Lawsuit Report
sources.description: 22.6% of H1 2025 US web-accessibility lawsuit filings (456 of ~2,000+) targeted sites with an accessibility overlay/widget installed; overlay presence is increasingly cited in complaints as evidence of awareness without adequate remediation. Basis for the skill's overlay-warning guidance.

sources.title: FTC Final Order — AccessiBe
sources.description: FTC fined AccessiBe $1,000,000 (final order approved April 2025) for false, misleading, or unsubstantiated advertising claims about automated WCAG/ADA compliance, and barred future compliance claims without evidence. Cite as grounds for not recommending overlay products as a compliance solution.

sources.title: WebAIM Screen Reader User Survey #10
sources.description: Fielded Dec 2023-Jan 2024, published Feb 2024, 1,539 respondents — the latest published edition as of 2026-07-11 (Survey #11 was in the field, results not yet published). Desktop primary share: JAWS 41%, NVDA 38%, VoiceOver 8.2%. Commonly-used desktop share: NVDA 65.6%, JAWS 60.5%, VoiceOver 43.9%. Mobile: VoiceOver 70.6%, TalkBack 34.6%. JAWS leads NVDA in North America/Australia; NVDA leads elsewhere.

sources.description: ESLint plugin providing static accessibility linting rules for JSX — catches missing alt text, label associations, keyboard-interaction issues, and ARIA errors at build time
